implementation_notes: respond_to(&block) collects one response per format - format.html renders the ERB/Jbuilder template, format.json { render json: ... }, format.xml, format.js, plus Mime::Type.register custom types - and negotiates them against the request's Accept header, while request.variant (:phone, :tablet, :desktop) lets one model select per-channel HTML templates. The format table plus Rails' template lookup (show.html.erb beside show.json.jbuilder) replaces the classic view registry, and render json:/render xml: are the serialization paths. The classic attached-observer structure is only relevant outside the request cycle (ActionCable broadcasts or a background job updating several representations).
code_sketch:
def show
  @movie = Movie.find(params[:id])          # one model
  respond_to do |format|
    format.html                               # app/views/movies/show.html.erb
    format.json { render json: @movie }       # or show.json.jbuilder
    format.xml  { render xml: @movie }
  end
end
pitfalls: respond_to raises ActionController::UnknownFormat for an unsupported media type; without a rescue_from the caller sees a 500 instead of a 406-style answer.
An action that omits respond_to implicitly answers every format with HTML, so a JSON client receives text/html rather than an error.
to_json/as_json cascade through associations unless the representation is restricted per format, which leaks attributes the HTML view never showed.
